output.summary: KEP-2336 proposes adding an optional `resource` field to Kubernetes OwnerReferences so garbage collection can identify the referent's REST resource directly, instead of deriving it from `kind` through discovery. Status is implementable, stage alpha, since 2021-02-09.
output.rationale: Today OwnerReferences carry only `kind`, and mapping kind to a URL requires a discovery sweep of upwards of 20 calls that is inefficient and fragile under network partitions. The KEP adds an optional `resource` field that, when set, is treated as authoritative with no lookup; when unset, `kind` is used as before, so existing clients keep working. The only behavioral change is for new clusters where both fields are set. The discussion records only an approval comment from wojtek-t on the PR, so the sources do not give a detailed reasoning trail beyond the design document.

alternatives.why_not: Per the design doc, this doesn't solve the network partition issue.
The doc says the existing cache doesn't cover all cases like cold starts and expired data.

alternatives.option: Stop looking for RESTMappings once any match is found
alternatives.why_not: The doc says this results in missing the intended referent in multi-match cases and doesn't solve cold starts and expired data.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes adding an optional `resource` field to OwnerReferences. If provided, this will be the authoritative value and no lookup or approximation of user intent will be required.
If not provided, the `kind` will be used as it is today. If both are provided, old clusters continue to work and new clusters will be more efficient and resilient.
In this case, the new cluster does not have to perform any lookups and will trust the client's specification of `resource`.
This doesn't solve the network partition issue.
